主要内容: As the US debt grows, here are 23 debt-free companies. CNBC research shows that only about 23 companies in the S&P 500 have managed to stay debt-free. When looking at the year-to-date stock performance, only eight of these names are outperforming the S&P 500. These companies include Chipotle (CMG), MasterCard (MA), Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY), Paychex (PAYX), Visa (V), Akamai (AKAM), Robert Half (RHI), and Forest Labs (FRX). Among these, Mastercard, Paychex, Visa, and Robert Half all pay a dividend. Lazard Capital's Managing Director Art Hogan notes that having no debt isn't necessarily a big plus for a company and that it is actually a favorable time for companies to take on debt. He adds that companies continue to have reasonable debt-to-equity ratios and that most of the selling pressure seen in this current uncertainty has been agnostic of debt levels. Debt-Free Companies include: Chipotle (CMG), MasterCard (MA), Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY), Paychex (PAYX), Visa (V), Akamai (AKAM), Robert Half (RHI), Forest Labs (FRX), Garmin (GRMN), Cognizant Technology (CTSH), T. Rowe Price (TROW), LSI Corp. (LSI), Expeditors Intl. (EXPD), Monster Beverage (MNST), News Corp. (NWSA), Fastenal (FAST), Quanta Services (PWR), Coach (COH), Urban Outfitters (URBN), F5 Networks (FFIV), Citrix Systems (CTXS), Red Hat (RHT), Intuitive Surgical (ISRG). About half of these companies are from the technology sector, which has the lowest debt-to-total assets ratio at about 16 percent. Other sectors with low debt include Financials (23 percent), Energy (24 percent), and Industrials (26 percent). In contrast, sectors like Telecom, Utilities, and Consumer Staples have the highest debt-to-total assets ratios at 46 percent, 36 percent, and 34 percent, respectively. Analysts suggest that some companies in these defensive sectors, which tend to generate steady cash, offer high dividend yields and thus take on debt to fund these payouts.
